raw.body:
﻿Hey @JHON12091986, thanks for digging into this. Your root-cause analysis is correct: the crash comes from `String.fromCharCode.apply` spreading every byte as a separate argument and exceeding the engine argument limit.

Heads up so we avoid duplicate effort: there are already two open PRs implementing exactly this chunked fix, #36936 and #36941, so the change itself is likely covered.

One note on your snippet if you keep iterating: `CHUNK_SIZE = 65536` sits right at the edge of the per-call argument limit. On some engines (historically JavaScriptCore/Safari) that cap is around 65536 or lower, so a chunk of exactly 65536 can still throw the same `RangeError`. The `if (uint8.length <= 65536)` fast path has the same risk. A safer, conventional value is `0x8000` (32768). Minor: `uint8.subarray(...)` is a zero-copy view, while `.slice(...)` copies each chunk.

Also worth framing it as "handle large buffers correctly" rather than "validate/reject" them, since a large binary value is legitimate here and just needs to be converted.
